name: The Storymaker’s Journal
label: Creative writing journal for kids
title: The Storymaker’s Journal: creative writing and drawing prompts for kids | Mazo Moon
description: A story-writing journal for children: build characters, map worlds, try comic challenges and story starters. 110 pages of prompts, 6 × 9 in, by Mazo Moon.
h1: Every story starts with one small idea
lead: Draw, imagine and create your own adventures, one prompt at a time.
for: For children who are full of ideas but stuck at a blank page
For doodlers, daydreamers and comic fans
For quiet afternoons, half term and long car journeys

p: Most children love making things up, until someone hands them a blank page and says “write a story”. Then the ideas vanish.
Starting is the hardest part. A whole story feels like too much, so they don’t start at all.

approach.h: Build the story in small pieces
p: Instead of asking for a whole story, this journal starts small: invent a character, draw a map, try a comic challenge. Bit by bit, they collect the pieces of a story without noticing.
Then they turn their favourite idea into a story of their very own. Some pages are marked TOGETHER, for doing side by side with a grown-up.

offer.p: Prompts that do the hard part, starting, so the fun part can take over.
features: Profiles to fill in: what they’re good at, what scares them, what they want more than anything, their secret.
Maps to draw with mountains, rivers, towns and a secret hiding place, plus a map key.
How comics work, a sound effects bank to borrow from, and panels to fill.

gallery: Character Profile: draw them, then get to know them
Map My World, on a dotted grid
How Comics Work: panels, bubbles and sound effects
Sound Effects Bank: WHOOSH! SPLAT! KABOOM!

proof.p: A mix of drawing and writing, so it suits children who’d rather draw than write, and the other way round.
note: I made this for children with big imaginations who freeze at a blank page. Breaking a story into small, playful pieces takes the pressure off.
The pages can be done in any order, so they can follow whatever they’re excited about that day.

items: A welcome page and a “this book belongs to the storymaker” page
World maps with a map key
Comic challenges, tips and a sound effects bank
TOGETHER pages for a grown-up and child
110 pages in total, on cream paper

points: One paperback book, printed and posted by Amazon.
No subscription and nothing to download. Open it and start.
Amazon handles delivery and returns, just like anything else you buy there.

faq: It suits children from about seven to eleven. Younger children can draw their answers and do the TOGETHER pages with a grown-up.
My child doesn’t like writing. Will they enjoy it?
There’s plenty of drawing: characters, maps and comics. Many children end up writing more because they’ve got something they want to say.
How is it different from The Storymaker’s Comic Book?
This journal is about inventing characters, worlds and story ideas, with a little comic making. The Comic Book is A4 and is all comics: twelve to make from start to finish.
Do they need to do it in order?
No. Every page works on its own, so they can jump to whatever looks fun.
It isn’t a workbook, but the habits it builds, like planning a character or a setting, are the same ones used in creative writing at school.

close.p: Hand them the first small idea and see where it goes.
